copyAndSwapTips: Reference fields accept the same exported `Type:Name` text, so you can copy one in-game asset reference into another config.
Linked passive references are how you swap attached sub-effects. This is the clean route for cases like giving Firewave a different attached effect.

instructions: Edit quickEdit[].value for the simplest workflow, or use the raw overrides object if you want full control.
Use the simpleSettings section for the grouped quick overview of settings this mod can actually write.

uiCapabilities, guidedActions, librarySlots, librarySuggestions, collectionEditors, referenceChoices, iconChoices, and nativeUiPlacement are the launcher-facing hints that describe what the visual editor can safely do here.
operations.entries is for add/remove/replace/duplicate/clear actions that raw value overrides cannot express safely.
Use advanced.fields for the full readable list of captured values. Check the editable flag before relying on a path.
advanced.defaults contains the original values captured before any JSON overrides are applied.
operationStatus shows whether each semantic add/remove/replace/clear action was applied successfully on the last run.
overrideStatus shows whether each override in the file was applied successfully on the last run.
advanced.effectiveValues shows the currently active values after overrides were applied.
Copy a path from simpleSettings or advanced.effectiveValues into overrides and assign the new value there.
Use [index] for arrays and dot notation for fields and properties.
Exported members include public fields and Unity [SerializeField] private fields.
Direct JSON overrides are reliable for numbers, booleans, strings, and enums.

Unity object references can usually be reused by copying the exported Type:Name string back into overrides for that field. referenceChoices.availableReferences lists the best captured candidates when the launcher wants a picker.
Remove an entry from overrides to fall back to the game default.
